symptom: PC-A can reach devices in VLAN 10 but cannot reach the server in VLAN 20.
topology_note: PC-A is in VLAN 10; server is in VLAN 20; router-on-a-stick is used.
show_outputs:
show ip route
C 192.168.10.0/24 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/0.10
C 192.168.20.0/24 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/0.20
expected_fault: No inter-VLAN routing fault is indicated; the evidence shows both VLAN networks are routed. Investigate host/server ACL or endpoint configuration next.

symptom: PC-A is connected to the correct switch but receives connectivity only to the wrong department's devices.
topology_note: PC-A should belong to VLAN 10 (SALES); access port Fa0/5 is intended for SALES.
show_outputs:
show vlan brief
10 SALES active
20 HR active
show interfaces fa0/5 switchport
Access Mode VLAN: 20
expected_fault: Access port Fa0/5 is assigned to VLAN 20 instead of VLAN 10.

symptom: Two PCs on the same VLAN cannot communicate through the access switch.
topology_note: Both PCs should be in VLAN 30; one access port was recently changed.
show_outputs:
show vlan brief
30 USERS active
show interfaces fa0/7 switchport
Access Mode VLAN: 1
expected_fault: Fa0/7 is in the default VLAN instead of VLAN 30.

symptom: A host in VLAN 20 cannot communicate through the trunk to the router.
topology_note: Switch-to-router link uses Gi0/1 as an 802.1Q trunk.
show_outputs:
show interfaces trunk
Port Gi0/1
Vlans allowed on trunk: 10,30
show vlan brief
20 SERVERS active
expected_fault: VLAN 20 is not allowed on the trunk.

symptom: VLAN 40 exists on one switch but hosts in VLAN 40 cannot reach hosts on the second switch.
topology_note: Two switches are connected by a trunk; VLAN 40 should span both switches.
show_outputs:
show interfaces trunk
Vlans allowed on trunk: 10,20,30
show vlan brief
40 GUEST active
expected_fault: VLAN 40 is missing from the trunk's allowed VLAN list.

symptom: PC receives an IP address but cannot reach its local router gateway.
topology_note: PC is in subnet 192.168.10.0/24; gateway should be 192.168.10.1.
show_outputs:
ipconfig
IPv4 Address: 192.168.10.25
Subnet Mask: 255.255.255.0
Default Gateway: 192.168.20.1
expected_fault: Default gateway is outside the PC's subnet.

symptom: PC can ping another host on the same subnet but cannot reach remote networks.
topology_note: PC is correctly addressed in 192.168.5.0/24.
show_outputs:
ipconfig
IPv4: 192.168.5.20
Mask: 255.255.255.0
Default Gateway: 0.0.0.0
expected_fault: The PC has no default gateway configured.

symptom: Only one workstation has intermittent local connectivity while other hosts on the same VLAN work normally.
topology_note: PC should use 10.10.10.0/24.
show_outputs:
show ip interface brief (router)
Gi0/0 10.10.10.1 up up
PC ipconfig
IPv4: 10.10.10.55
Mask: 255.255.0.0
Gateway: 10.10.10.1
expected_fault: The host uses an incorrect subnet mask (/16 instead of /24), causing incorrect local/remote decisions.

symptom: PC can reach its gateway but cannot reach an external subnet.
topology_note: Gateway interface is operational and connected to the LAN.
show_outputs:
show ip interface brief
Gi0/0 192.168.1.1 up up
show ip route
C 192.168.1.0/24 is directly connected
expected_fault: No route to the remote network is shown.

symptom: A server responds to some clients but not to a newly configured client.
show_outputs:
ipconfig (new client)
IPv4: 172.16.1.50
Mask: 255.255.255.0
Gateway: 172.16.1.1
show ip arp
Internet 172.16.1.50 - 0000.0000.0000
expected_fault: ARP information is incomplete for the client; investigate Layer 2 connectivity/interface status before changing routing.

symptom: Client automatically receives a 169.254.x.x address instead of a LAN address.
topology_note: Client is connected to the Users VLAN; DHCP server is on another subnet.
show_outputs:
ipconfig
IPv4 Address: 169.254.44.18
DHCP Enabled: Yes
show running-config interface vlan 10
no ip helper-address
expected_fault: DHCP relay configuration is missing on the Layer 3 interface.

symptom: Some clients receive addresses from the wrong network.
topology_note: VLAN 20 should use 192.168.20.0/24.
show_outputs:
show ip dhcp pool
Pool: USERS
Network 192.168.10.0 /24
Default router 192.168.10.1
expected_fault: The DHCP pool network and gateway do not match the intended VLAN 20 subnet.

symptom: DHCP clients receive addresses but cannot communicate outside their subnet.
topology_note: DHCP server should provide gateway 10.20.0.1.
show_outputs:
show ip dhcp pool USERS
Network 10.20.0.0 /24
Default router 10.20.0.254
expected_fault: The DHCP pool advertises the wrong default gateway.

symptom: New clients fail to obtain an address while existing clients continue working.
topology_note: DHCP pool is configured for 50 usable addresses.
show_outputs:
show ip dhcp pool USERS
Maximum addresses: 50
Leased addresses: 50
Excluded addresses: 2
expected_fault: The DHCP pool has no remaining available leases.

symptom: DHCP service is configured but clients in VLAN 30 do not receive leases.
topology_note: DHCP server is reachable from the router.
show_outputs:
show running-config interface g0/0.30
encapsulation dot1Q 30
ip address 10.30.0.1 255.255.255.0
show running-config | include helper
(no output)
expected_fault: The VLAN 30 interface lacks an ip helper-address when the DHCP server is remote.

symptom: Users can ping 8.8.8.8 but cannot open websites by name.
topology_note: Internet connectivity is otherwise working.
show_outputs:
ipconfig /all
DNS Servers: 0.0.0.0
ping 8.8.8.8
Reply from 8.8.8.8
expected_fault: DNS server is not configured on the client.

symptom: Clients resolve some internal names but cannot resolve external domain names.
topology_note: Internal DNS server is 10.1.1.10.
show_outputs:
nslookup example.com
Server: 10.1.1.10
*** 10.1.1.10 can't find example.com: SERVFAIL
show running-config | section ip name-server
ip name-server 10.1.1.10
expected_fault: DNS server is reachable but is failing external resolution; investigate DNS forwarding/recursion rather than routing.

symptom: A client resolves a hostname to an old IP address after a server migration.
topology_note: DNS record was recently changed from 10.0.0.20 to 10.0.0.30.
show_outputs:
nslookup app.local
Name: app.local
Address: 10.0.0.20
expected_fault: The DNS record still points to the old server address.

symptom: Only one PC cannot resolve internal hostnames; other PCs work.
topology_note: All PCs use the same LAN DNS server.
show_outputs:
ipconfig /all
DNS Servers: 192.168.50.99
ping 192.168.50.10
Request timed out
expected_fault: The affected PC has an incorrect/unreachable DNS server address.

symptom: DNS queries fail even though the DNS server interface is configured.
topology_note: DNS server is expected at 192.168.10.53.
show_outputs:
show ip interface brief
Gi0/1 192.168.10.1 up up
show access-lists
access-list 101 deny udp any host 192.168.10.53 eq domain
access-list 101 permit ip any any
expected_fault: An ACL explicitly blocks UDP DNS traffic to the DNS server.

symptom: Branch A can reach its directly connected LAN but cannot reach Branch B.
topology_note: Two routers are connected through 10.0.0.0/30.
show_outputs:
show ip route
C 192.168.1.0/24 is directly connected
C 10.0.0.0/30 is directly connected
expected_fault: No route to Branch B's 192.168.2.0/24 network is present.

symptom: A route exists, but traffic is sent toward the wrong next hop.
topology_note: Branch B network is 192.168.2.0/24; correct next hop is 10.0.0.2.
show_outputs:
show ip route 192.168.2.0
Routing entry for 192.168.2.0/24
via 10.0.0.6
expected_fault: Configured next hop does not match the intended topology.

symptom: A router has a route to a destination but the route is not installed as expected.
topology_note: Static route should use next hop 10.0.0.2.
show_outputs:
show ip route 192.168.2.0
% Network not in table
show ip interface brief
Gi0/1 10.0.0.1 up down
expected_fault: The next-hop interface is operationally down, preventing the expected path.

symptom: OSPF neighbors are not forming between two directly connected routers.
topology_note: Routers share 10.0.0.0/30 and should form an OSPF adjacency.
show_outputs:
show ip ospf neighbor
(no neighbors)
show ip ospf interface g0/0
Network Type: BROADCAST
show running-config interface g0/0
ip ospf 1 area 0
expected_fault: The evidence alone is insufficient to identify the exact cause; check IP addressing, OSPF area, timers, and interface state.

symptom: A remote network is reachable from one router but not from another.
topology_note: Three routers form a chain; routing should be learned dynamically.
show_outputs:
show ip route 172.16.30.0
% Network not in table
show ip ospf neighbor
Neighbor 10.0.0.2 FULL
expected_fault: The router lacks a route to the remote network despite an OSPF neighbor; investigate route advertisement/network statements.

symptom: Employees can access the internal server, but the guest subnet cannot.
topology_note: Guest network is 192.168.50.0/24; server is 192.168.10.10.
show_outputs:
show access-lists
10 deny ip 192.168.50.0 0.0.0.255 host 192.168.10.10
20 permit ip any any
expected_fault: ACL intentionally blocks guest-to-server traffic.

symptom: Users cannot access HTTPS services, but ICMP ping works.
topology_note: Web server is 10.10.10.20.
show_outputs:
show access-lists
101 deny tcp any host 10.10.10.20 eq 443
102 permit icmp any any
expected_fault: ACL blocks TCP/443 while permitting ICMP.

symptom: All traffic from a subnet is unexpectedly blocked after an ACL change.
topology_note: Subnet is 10.5.0.0/24.
show_outputs:
show access-lists
100 deny ip 10.5.0.0 0.0.0.255 any
110 permit ip any any
expected_fault: The first ACL entry denies all traffic from the affected subnet.

symptom: A newly created VLAN cannot access the internet while older VLANs can.
topology_note: VLAN 40 uses 10.40.0.0/24; internet access is controlled by an outbound ACL.
show_outputs:
show access-lists
120 permit ip 10.10.0.0 0.0.0.255 any
130 permit ip 10.20.0.0 0.0.0.255 any
(no entry for 10.40.0.0/24)
expected_fault: The ACL has no permit entry for the new VLAN, so implicit deny may block it.

symptom: An administrator can reach the router but cannot reach the management SSH service.
topology_note: SSH server is the router itself; management subnet is 192.168.100.0/24.
show_outputs:
show access-lists
150 deny tcp 192.168.100.0 0.0.0.255 any eq 22
160 permit ip any any
expected_fault: The ACL denies SSH traffic from the management subnet.

symptom: Inside hosts can reach the gateway but cannot access the internet.
topology_note: Inside subnet is 192.168.1.0/24; public interface is Gi0/1.
show_outputs:
show ip nat translations
Pro Inside global Inside local Outside local Outside global
(no entries)
show running-config | include ip nat
expected_fault: No NAT configuration is shown for the inside subnet.

symptom: NAT is configured, but translations are not created when users browse externally.
topology_note: Inside interface is Gi0/0; outside is Gi0/1.
show_outputs:
show running-config interface g0/0
ip nat inside
show running-config interface g0/1
(no ip nat outside)
expected_fault: The outside interface lacks the required ip nat outside designation.

symptom: Users receive public translations, but internet traffic does not return correctly.
topology_note: Inside subnet is 10.1.0.0/24.
show_outputs:
show ip nat translations
10.1.0.20 -> 203.0.113.20
show ip route 0.0.0.0
% Network not in table
expected_fault: NAT is occurring, but the router lacks a default route to the internet.

symptom: Only some inside hosts are translated; others cannot access external services.
topology_note: NAT should cover 192.168.10.0/24.
show_outputs:
show access-lists 1
Standard IP access list 1
10 permit 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.127
show ip nat statistics
Inside local addresses not translated: 192.168.10.150
expected_fault: NAT ACL covers only part of the inside subnet.

symptom: A public server cannot be reached using its public IP from outside.
topology_note: Internal server is 10.10.10.50; public address should be 203.0.113.50.
show_outputs:
show running-config | include ip nat inside source static
(no output)
expected_fault: No static NAT/port-forward mapping is configured for the server.

symptom: Wireless clients connect to the SSID but cannot obtain an IP address.
topology_note: SSID USERS maps to VLAN 20; DHCP service is available for VLAN 20.
show_outputs:
show wlan summary
SSID USERS
show vlan brief
20 USERS active
show ip interface brief
Vlan20 192.168.20.1 up up
expected_fault: The evidence does not show a DHCP failure; investigate WLAN-to-VLAN mapping and DHCP relay/client association details next.

symptom: Guest wireless users can access an internal database server.
topology_note: Guest SSID should be isolated from internal VLAN 10.
show_outputs:
show access-lists
200 permit ip 192.168.50.0 0.0.0.255 10.10.10.0 0.0.0.255
210 permit ip any any
expected_fault: ACL explicitly permits guest-to-internal traffic, violating guest isolation policy.

symptom: Wireless clients repeatedly disconnect from the network while wired clients remain stable.
topology_note: AP is connected to the switch and powered.
show_outputs:
show interfaces gigabitEthernet0/2
GigabitEthernet0/2 is up, line protocol is up
show wlan summary
SSID CAMPUS
expected_fault: Evidence confirms the wired uplink is up but does not identify the wireless cause; investigate RF/channel utilization, authentication logs, and AP events.

symptom: Users see the corporate SSID but authentication fails for all users.
topology_note: WLAN uses WPA2-Enterprise with a RADIUS server at 10.100.0.10.
show_outputs:
show radius statistics
Server 10.100.0.10
Requests: 0
show ip route 10.100.0.0
% Network not in table
expected_fault: The wireless controller has no route to the RADIUS server network.

symptom: Guest Wi-Fi clients receive an IP address but can reach internal hosts.
topology_note: Guest subnet is 172.20.0.0/24 and should be internet-only.
show_outputs:
ipconfig
IPv4: 172.20.0.25
Gateway: 172.20.0.1
show access-lists
(no guest isolation ACL)
show ip route 10.10.0.0
Routing entry present
expected_fault: Guest clients are routed to internal networks and no isolation ACL is present.
